scores: Reviewers: creative director 4.5, UX 4.5, copy 5.0 (mean 4.7/10). The credibility review arrived cut off mid-finding with no score, and the fifth review is missing from the input. Every review judged the home page only. I checked the rest on the live site. The line, product, color and lighting views (hash routes such as #speakers, #speaker-poison, #colour-poison and #lighting, which no review saw) rate about 6/10. They have one studio lineup on one ground, a spec table with named drivers, a fabrication drawing, a gallery captioned 'Render', and color pairings. They are held back by pairings that recommend a speaker for a speaker, the old Mantle and corded Core, mixed backgrounds, mono labels and British spelling. The site as it stands: about 5/10. My estimates: about 6.5 after the no-regret fixes on today's pictures, and 8 or better with the recommended direction and the new picture set.
no_regret_fixes: One picture set, one shot bible, one swap. Write a one-page shot bible and render the new Tropos (smooth horn, white lines, uplit base), the cordless Core and the new Mantle to it. STUDIO, for every product picture: a seamless in the page's own paper (#F4F1EC) so the frame edge disappears, one large soft key light high left with a weak fill, camera at product mid-height, about an 85 mm lens, product about 70% of frame height. For tinted material in light, study Sabine Marcelis's photographs of her resin work. NIGHT: the uplit board-formed concrete set already used in the light section. WORLD: every habitat in one film grade (filmic curve, fine grain, real depth of field, haze). Run all three through one color pipeline so Ember is the same red everywhere. Render in this order: the hero lineup (16:9, plus a separately composed phone frame); the eight uplit singles and the uplit eight; the turning view; studio singles of each product in all eight colors, front and three-quarter; six close-ups (horn mouth, edge glow, uplit base, joinery, back mark, coin); the room. Retire the meadow, the peach gradient, the white Mantle packshot, the corded Core and the old Mantle in the room. Never mix old and new horns on the site: until a product's new pictures exist, show a type-only tile, never the superseded design. Before release, check all eight colors for identical parts (handles, woofer ring, base light), per the founder's own 'some don't have handles' note.

Ship the language already decided, now, on today's pictures. 'A world of sound, in color.' replaces 'Something in the air.' everywhere, including the speaker page's 'Eight things in the air.'. Use American English in every view, alt text and meta/og tag ('colour' appears 11 times on the home alone): Colors; Contact for Enquire/Enquiries; dealers for stockists; microfiber. Put inches first ('51 in (1293 mm)') and use one name per thing ('Mantle, a turntable', never 'record player'). Delete every mono eyebrow and every 'See the …' link; the product's name is the link. Drop the 'eight colours'/'acrylic' refrain ('eight' at most once a page) and every line that only describes its own picture: 'Tropos is a horn loudspeaker cast in tinted acrylic, in eight colours from Ember to Smoke.', 'One acrylic, three ways to use it.', 'Eight colours, every line.', 'Covers on, by a tall window.' and 'From launch, write here for prices and lead times.'. Keep the eight color lines, 'The oldest amplifier is a shape.', 'A pair in Poison.', 'Write to us.' and 'Everything is made to order, so we quote rather than list.'. House rules: at most one 'X, so Y' sentence and one colon a page, and no words about the interface. Add a build check that fails on colour, enquir, stockist, microfibre or 'Something in the air'.

Keep the light stage's idea (the founder likes it) and fix how it feels. I checked the pin in Chromium at 1440×900 and 390×844, and it holds. The reviewers' black screens are what every full-page capture, print and failed pin shows. The real faults are a run of 2.9 screens, a picture feathered into half the frame, Smoke holding for most of the last screen, and an untidy exit where the coin row slides up under the header. Rebuild it as one 100svh frame, minus the header. Run the uplit picture full-bleed (cover, horn never cropped, a 9:16 crop on phones), with the color's name and line over it at lower left. Put the coins inside the frame at lower right, still a radio group, but clickable and arrow-keyed too. Cut the run to 8 × 20svh (about 1.6 screens), keep the off-then-on change between colors, and open the last step onto the uplit eight at full height. The static version (no JS, reduced motion, print, captures) is the uplit eight with the eight names and lines beneath. Take coin colors from the shared tokens; here Fog currently shows as mid-gray and Smoke as black. Copy: keep 'Put a light under it.' and answer it with 'We did.' once the new uplit base is pictured; cut the explainer sentence and 'TROPOS 01'. Don't adopt the UX reviewer's unpinned auto-advance: it hides seven colors behind a timer and needs a pause control (WCAG 2.2.2).

Make the close collect interest. Under 'Write to us.' and 'Everything is made to order, so we quote rather than list.', add a short form: email (required), the eight coins as an optional multi-select, an optional 'For: home / trade / press', a message and one 'Send' button. Post it to a Vercel function that stores each entry (email, colors, product, role, date, source page) and notifies hello@earf.world. Confirm with 'Noted. We'll write when there's something to hear.' Set hello@earf.world beneath as a plain mailto link in the body face, with no mono and no 'Copy address' pill. The product page's 'Enquire about a pair' becomes 'Ask about Tropos in Poison' and opens the same form, pre-filled. Add a one-field 'News, rarely.' sign-up in the footer, a one-line privacy note with a short /privacy page, and Vercel Web Analytics. Report sign-ups by color every week: that's the first demand number investors will ask for, and it sets the order for the first dye lots.

Make the hero one 100svh frame. Stand the lineup on one clean line or on the founder's arc (today the feet zigzag by up to 40 px), filling about 55% of the frame's height, with 'A world of sound, in color.' in the picture's quiet upper third. Sample the page color from the render so the gray seam behind the horns disappears. Add one small caption, 'Hi-fi and lighting, designed in San Francisco.', with 'Render' at lower right. Set each color's name small at its speaker's foot, and make each speaker a link to Tropos in that color; this replaces the dot legend. Delete the 'EARF · TROPOS' eyebrow, the explainer sentence, both pill buttons, the legend and the disclaimer. Recompose the phone's hero-portrait.jpg as its own frame (two rows of four or a tight arc, each speaker at least 80 px wide; today they are about 50 px). Build the layout now on the current picture and drop in the new lineup once it's rendered.

Make the pairings follow the founder's rule. Today the page for Tropos in Poison recommends Tropos in Ember ('Complementary') and Tropos in Acid and Ice ('Analogous'). That is a speaker recommended for a speaker, which the founder explicitly ruled out. On a product page, recommend only the other lines: Mantle in the same color a shade deeper (monochromatic), and Hemisphere and Core in the opposite color (complementary). Keep the full range on the color pages.

Give the pages that already exist real addresses. The line, product, color and lighting pages the founder asked for are built, with breadcrumbs, a gallery, coins and specs. But they live as hash views inside one 197 KB document, so every shared link previews as 'EARF · Tropos' with the home's picture, and no review saw them. Have web.py write static pages at /tropos, /tropos/{color}, /lighting, /mantle, /colors/{color} and /contact, plus slots for /studio, /journal and /press. Give each page its own title, description and og:image showing that product in that color. Map the old hashes to the new paths, and keep noindex until launch. Nav: Tropos · Lighting · Mantle · Colors · Studio, with Contact set apart at the right. On phones, 'Menu' becomes plain text that opens a full-screen sheet with the products as pictures. Footer: the products; Studio (Progress, plus Journal and Press once released); Contact (email, and Instagram once there is one); 'News, rarely.'; one legal line in sentence case. Until the new Mantle is rendered, /mantle is one quiet screen of type.

Show the palette once on the home and define it once. Delete the dot legend under the hero and the 'By colour' chapter, and move that chapter's one good idea (a room can be one color or three) into the room's caption. Define the eight colors as tokens: a value sampled from the lit render, a rendered coin at 24 px and up, a flat dot below that size, and a hairline ring on Fog so it holds on paper. Use only those tokens everywhere: light stage, product and color pages, loader. Re-render the coins so each has its own reflection; the founder's note that every coin carries the same square highlight still applies. Give coins hit areas of at least 44 px, and show the color's name and line on the selected coin.

Swap the startup kit for a design house's. Pill buttons ('See the speakers', 'Copy address', 'Menu') become text links in the body face, underlined at 1 px with a 4 px offset. Drop monospace everywhere except spec tables, and drop rounded image corners, gray caption panels and chevrons on pictures; captions sit on the page ground. Keep one family (Instrument Sans) but give it real contrast. Make the hero line the largest type on the site: today the light stage's color name (up to 96 px; 95 px at 1440 wide, 56 px on a phone) is bigger than the hero (up to 80 px; 72 px at 1440 wide, 32 px on a phone). Use display size for three moments only, text at 18 px and captions at 13 px. Space everything on three steps: 0 between pictures, about 160 px from picture to text, about 240 px between chapters. Warm the night ground from blue-black #0B0C10 to a near-black in the paper's hue (about #13110F), and use it for the dark opening too. Shrink the header lockup by about 20% and serve the globe at 3×. No new typeface for now.

Put sound on the home where the founder asked for it: 'the cool 360 view' straight after the hero. Tropos turns slowly on the studio seamless, with no instructions, under 'The oldest amplifier is a shape.'. Set three design figures large, taken from the existing particulars and re-checked against the new horn: to about 51 Hz, up to about 115 dB at 1 m, and 2 × 125 W built in. Footnote them 'Design figures; measured ones follow with the first pair' and link to the horn chapter on /tropos. Today all of this sits only on the speaker page, and the home page of a hi-fi brand never once says 'sound'.

Add proof of making as one Studio beat before the close. Bring in the fabrication drawing that is already on the speaker page. Turn Progress into a dated line (Drawn: done; First pair: in progress; Measured: next), stamped 'Updated [date]' and kept current. As soon as the acrylic chips and off-cuts the founder approved arrive, add the site's first real photograph: the eight colors held up to window light. Add one line on the name. Add the founder's name and one signed sentence only if the founder wants to be named. Build slots now for the press kit and journal that are on hold, and publish them only when the founder says so.

Take the habitats out of the carousel chrome, whatever form they end up in. No chevron on the picture and no white fade over the next slide. Caption each with its line ('Ember. The last light of the fire.'), show a quiet '1 / 8', and use native swipe with scroll-snap on phones. Hold back any frame that still reads as CG (today Ember's lava and the smeared Dust mesa) until it passes the WORLD grade.

Slim the phone page and art-direct it for the phone. At load, a phone downloads the same 2.8 MB as a desktop: 31 images, including the light stage's 1600 px JPEGs at up to 300 KB each. The opening covers the page until about 2.3 s on a phone and 2.8 s on a desktop, even on a fast connection. Use srcset with phone-sized AVIF/WebP, preload only the hero and the first light frame, and load the rest as the visitor approaches. Keep the opening the founder designed, but end it as soon as the hero image has loaded and play it once per session. The header globe keeps turning, as the founder wants, and stands still for reduced motion. Run product tiles full width (product at 80% or more of the screen width), and give product pages a sticky 'Tropos · Poison · Ask' bar. Test in iOS Safari and Instagram's in-app browser.

Say 'render' quietly, once per picture. Put 'Render' in each caption (the product gallery's '1 / 11 · Render' already does this) and one sentence-case footer line: 'Designed in San Francisco. Pictures are renders until the first pair is built.' Delete the line under the hero and the uppercase mono footer. When the room is re-rendered, set Poison at its true daylight density (matched to a real chip once the chips arrive), run the cables behind the cabinets to an outlet out of frame, show the new Mantle, and run the picture full-bleed with 'A pair in Poison.' and '51 in (1293 mm) tall' as its only caption.

directions.name: Launch film: one picture per screen
directions.idea: The home works like Apple's page for a new product, made by a design house. Each screen holds one full-bleed picture and at most one line, in an order that builds: the lineup, the sound, the light, the worlds, a room, the rest of the family, the proof, then contact. The habitats become the spine, because 'A world of sound, in color.', the name EARF and the globe all promise a world for each color. The product and color pages the founder asked for stay underneath as the store.
directions.references: apple.com/imac (the 2021 color launch): the lineup hero, color swapping the picture in place, one idea per screen, disclosures as footnotes. bang-olufsen.com, the Beolab 90 and Beolab 50 pages: the product at architectural scale, and sound told one figure at a time. aesop.com: dry lines said once, captions doing the work, text links instead of buttons.
directions.what_changes: Home order: the lineup with the tagline → Sound (Tropos turning, 'The oldest amplifier is a shape.', three figures) → After dark (the one-screen light stage, ending on the uplit eight) → The world (the eight habitats full-bleed, each with its line, or a gutterless 4 × 2 mosaic that opens full-screen if eight screens is too long; a natural place for the Mother EARF promise the founder chose) → At home (the room) → Hemisphere and the cordless Core in one frame, 'One hangs. One wanders.' → Mantle, once rendered → Studio (drawing, chips, dated progress) → Write to us, under one last picture of the pair uplit at dusk. About 10 to 12 screens, one line each. The product cards, 'By colour', the legend and the carousel go. /tropos keeps the gallery, coins, horn chapter, particulars and drawing, and each /colors page carries its habitat and pairings.
directions.risk: It lives or dies on the pictures. It needs the new speaker set, the turning view and all eight habitats at film grade, and today at least two habitats (Ember's lava, the Dust mesa) read as CG. A long page led by pictures feels slow wherever a screen is a pause rather than a picture, which is the founder's complaint about the light section. It is also heavy on phones unless images are managed tightly. It can't fully ship before the render set exists, so it goes out in two drops: structure and words now, then every picture in one swap.

directions.name: Color library: the eight as the way in
directions.idea: Color is the interface and the navigation. Each of the eight colors gets a numbered page with its world, its line, every product in that color, the founder's pairings and a physical sample to ask for. The home is a short store window where one row of coins recolors everything on it.
directions.references: apple.com/imac: a picker that changes the product where it stands. farrow-ball.com: every color a named, numbered page with a short story, suggested pairings and a sample you can order. teenage.engineering, the OP–1 field and OB–4 pages: plain studio photography on one ground and deadpan spec pages.
directions.what_changes: A home of about seven screens: the named lineup; Tropos turning, with its three figures; the uplit eight; three product tiles; one color chapter, where choosing a coin fills the screen with that color's habitat and line and recolors Tropos, the lamps and Mantle below it; the room; sign-up. The chosen color carries across pages in the URL (/tropos/poison) and pre-fills the form. The light stage moves to /tropos, where the uplit base is a feature. /colors/{color} becomes a destination with 'Ask for a sample' for trade and press: the acrylic coin, or the engraved, reeded-edge EARFcoin the founder picked. The habitats leave the home for the color pages.
directions.risk: It multiplies the renders needed (four products × eight colors × several views, of three designs not yet rendered) before the new set exists. A store with nothing to buy and no prices can feel hollow or premature. Samples mean making and posting physical things. And it demotes the habitats, the founder's biggest investment in pictures, to sub-pages.

directions.name: Open studio: the road to the first pair
directions.idea: The site is the studio's dispatch on the way to the first pair. It opens on the reveal, then shows the work in dated entries: the drawings, the simulated horn, the acrylic in hand, the first pair on the bench. The founder is named, and 'News, rarely.' is the main action. Belief comes from evidence, not polish.
directions.references: teenage.engineering: exploded drawings, field guides, and a dry voice that makes hardware lovable. vitsoe.com: a company that says plainly how and why it makes things. play.date (Panic's Playdate): dated updates in a deadpan voice that built a waiting list long before anything shipped.
directions.what_changes: Home: the hero; Tropos turning; 'Where Tropos stands' as a dated timeline with an artifact per step (the fabrication drawing, the horn's simulated response, the chips in window light, the first pair being built); the latest journal entries; the range as a compact row; sign-up with an optional color. Add /studio (the founder, the name, why a horn, why cast acrylic, the people involved), /press with the kit, and a journal updated every two weeks. The habitats appear as journal entries ('Where Poison began').
directions.risk: It rests on artifacts that don't exist yet (no chips photographed, no first pair), and on the founder releasing the held journal and press kit and agreeing to be named. A dispatch that goes quiet, or a date that slips in public, reads as a company in trouble. It has the least polish of the three for a brand meant to be 'world' class, and it puts today's renders of the old designs beside real work.

recommended: Launch film (direction 1), built on the product and color pages that already exist, with Studio as one beat. There are four reasons. First, it's what the founder asked for in their own words: Apple-style launch pictures, and 'a hero image that shows the whole cast of speakers in a creative way, and then the cool 360 view'. Second, it's the only direction that delivers 'A world of sound, in color.' with assets nobody else has: the lineup is color, the turning horn is sound, and the habitats and uplit concrete are the world. Third, the founder's e-commerce structure stays underneath, so nothing is given up. Direction 2's best parts are those product and color pages, and they only need real URLs and the pairing fix. Fourth, direction 3's best parts (the drawing, the chips, dated progress, the sign-up) are cheap no-regret fixes that fit into one Studio beat without making unfinished work the headline. Ship it in two drops. First, the words, light stage, hero layout, form, URLs, pairings and UI kit, on today's pictures minus the meadow, gradient and white packshot. Second, the new picture set, in one swap. One condition: a habitat that fails the WORLD grade stays off the home, and the mosaic shows only the ones that pass.
biggest_single_lever: The pictures. Render one new set to one shot bible (STUDIO on the page's own paper, NIGHT on the uplit concrete, WORLD for the habitats, one color pipeline) and swap it in all at once. The set is: the hero lineup in desktop and phone frames, the uplit eight, the turning view, studio singles in all eight colors, close-ups, the room and the graded habitats. Every picture on the site is a render, every speaker in them is the outgoing design, and they come from about seven unrelated briefs. Copy and layout fixes raise the floor, but only one coherent set of pictures of the current products makes EARF look like one world-class family. The new speaker isn't rendered yet, so this is also the critical path: start it now, and build everything else so the new pictures drop straight in.
